raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Purpose

Fixes #64652.

In the V2 model runner, EAGLE draft acceptance collapses after the first position whenever the target's backends need smaller kernel blocks than `--block-size`. For example, MiniMax-M3's sparse attention only runs 128-token pages, so this happens at `--block-size 256/512` on GB200.

**Cause:** the target model runner picks one kernel block size per KV cache group across all of that group's backends (`init_attn_backend` → `prepare_kernel_block_sizes`), and the KV cache is laid out in those kernel blocks. `DraftModelSpeculator.set_attn` then calls `init_attn_backend` again with only the draft layers. That re-selects the kernel block size from the draft backend alone and discards the result (`_`).

On GB200, FlashInfer (and Triton) accept the full 512-token block, so the draft's attention groups get no kernel split. Logged on the MiniMax-M3 repro at `--block-size 512`:

```
target group FLASHINFER          kernel_block_size 128
target group MINIMAX_M3_SPARSE   kernel_block_size 128
draft  group FLASHINFER          kernel_block_size None   # reads 512-token pages
```

Draft prefill reuses the target's attention metadata, so draft position 1 is correct. Draft decode steps 2+ build metadata from the draft's own groups and read the cache with the wrong page size, so their proposals are almost never accepted.

**Fix:** `init_attn_backend` takes optional `kernel_block_sizes`. `set_attn` passes `prepare_kernel_block_sizes(kv_cache_config, target_attn_groups)`, so the drafter uses the same selection policy as the target (including block-outermost packed caches, which keep the allocation's block size).

## Test Plan

- New unit test `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_attn_utils_kernel_block_size.py`: a 512-token group whose target backend only supports 128 and whose draft backend also supports 512. It checks that the draft keeps 128 when selected from the target's groups, and that with a block-outermost packed cache the draft gets the 512 allocation size.
- End-to-end on 1× GB200 (4 GPUs), `nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` TP2 + `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA` (3 speculative tokens), using the repro from #64652 (48 coding requests, concurrency 2).

## Test Result

Unit tests: both pass on H100 with the PR's sources over the latest nightly image (0.33.0rc1.dev573). `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py` gives 84 passed with or without this PR; its 10 DeepSeek-V4 cases fail on a circular import in both runs, which comes from loading the source over the image.

Accepted share at draft positions 1 / 2 / 3:

| `--block-size` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 512 | 0.83 / 0.16 / 0.03 | 0.80 / 0.62 / 0.48 |
| 128 (control) | 0.80 / 0.63 / 0.48 | — |

After the fix the draft's FlashInfer group logs `kernel_block_size 128`. Without the fix, a small dense model (Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 on H100, `--block-size` 64/128/256) already gives identical acceptance at every block size, because its target and draft pick the same kernel block size.

<details>
<summary>AI assistance</summary>

Root-caused, written and tested with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5). A human reviewed the change before submission.

</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Suggested reusing the existing allocation-size selection helper to keep this fix small and preserve packed-cache behavior. This is an AI-assisted code review; validation was limited to code inspection and synthetic selection checks.

Could we reuse the existing allocation-size selection helper here? For block-outermost packed caches, `prepare_kernel_block_sizes()` deliberately keeps manager-sized blocks, while `AttentionGroup.create_metadata_builders()` can choose a smaller kernel size for an individual backend. That means `groups[0].kernel_block_size` need not be the size used to allocate this KV group.

`target_attn_groups` already contains the full set of backends used by the runner, so this reuses the existing selection policy, including its packed-cache handling:

```suggestion
            kernel_block_sizes=prepare_kernel_block_sizes(
                kv_cache_config, target_attn_groups
            ),
```

Also extend the existing import in this file:

```python
from vllm.v1.worker.utils import AttentionGroup, prepare_kernel_block_sizes
```

A packed-cache regression case would help cover this distinction; the current test has `kv_cache_tensors=[]` and replaces `create_metadata_builders`, so it does not exercise the per-backend subdivision.

Validation scope: code inspection and a synthetic selection-only check using the original helper functions with stand-in backends/specs. The check showed a packed allocation of 512 with effective target/draft sizes of 128/512, where the first-group expression forwards 128. I have not reproduced a GPU serving failure for that configuration.

@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils as attn_utils
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    FullAttentionSpec,
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheGroupSpec,
+    KVCacheTensor,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.utils import AttentionGroup, prepare_kernel_block_sizes
+
+
+def _backend(name: str, sizes: list[int]):
+    class FakeBackend:
+        @staticmethod
+        def get_name() -> str:
+            return name
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def full_cls_name() -> tuple[str, str]:
+            return (__name__, name)
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def get_supported_kernel_block_sizes(kv_cache_spec=None) -> list[int]:
+            return sizes
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def supports_batch_invariance() -> bool:
+            return True
+
+    return FakeBackend
+
+
+# The target's backend only runs 128-token pages (like MiniMax-M3 sparse
+# attention); the draft's backend also runs the 512-token manager block.
+TARGET_BACKEND = _backend("TARGET", [128])
+DRAFT_BACKEND = _backend("DRAFT", [128, 512])
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def init(monkeypatch):
+    layers = {
+        "target": SimpleNamespace(get_attn_backend=lambda: TARGET_BACKEND, num_heads=8),
+        "draft": SimpleNamespace(get_attn_backend=lambda: DRAFT_BACKEND, num_heads=4),
+    }
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        attn_utils,
+        "get_layers_from_vllm_config",
+        lambda _config, _type, names=None: {
+            n: layers[n] for n in (names if names is not None else layers)
+        },
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(attn_utils, "get_shared_kv_cache_layers", lambda _c: {})
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        attn_utils,
+        "get_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_eligible_layers",
+        lambda _c, _d: set(),
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(attn_utils, "get_attn_cg_support", lambda _g, _c: None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(attn_utils, "get_num_ubatches", lambda _p: 1)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        AttentionGroup,
+        "create_metadata_builders",
+        lambda self, vllm_config, device, kernel_block_size=None, **_: setattr(
+            self, "kernel_block_size", kernel_block_size
+        ),
+    )
+
+    def run(packed=False, **kwargs):
+        spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=512, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=128, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        page = spec.page_size_bytes
+        # Block-outermost packing places both layers' pages inside each block.
+        tensors = (
+            [
+                KVCacheTensor(
+                    size=2 * page,
+                    layers=["target", "draft"],
+                    layer_stride=page,
+                    block_stride=2 * page,
+                )
+            ]
+            if packed
+            else []
+        )
+        kv_cache_config = KVCacheConfig(
+            num_blocks=1,
+            kv_cache_tensors=tensors,
+            kv_cache_groups=[
+                KVCacheGroupSpec(layer_names=["target", "draft"], kv_cache_spec=spec)
+            ],
+        )
+        vllm_config = SimpleNamespace(parallel_config=None)
+        groups, cg, sizes = attn_utils.init_attn_backend(
+            kv_cache_config, vllm_config, torch.device("cpu"), **kwargs
+        )
+        return groups, sizes, kv_cache_config
+
+    return run
+
+
+def test_draft_reuses_target_kernel_block_size(init):
+    # The target runner sees every layer of the group, so the cache is laid
+    # out in 128-token kernel blocks.
+    groups, target_sizes, kv_cache_config = init(draft_layer_names={"draft"})
+    assert target_sizes == [128]
+    assert {g.kernel_block_size for g in groups[0]} == {128}
+
+    # Seen alone, the draft's backend would pick 512 and read that cache with
+    # the wrong page size.
+    _, draft_only, _ = init(active_layer_names={"draft"})
+    assert draft_only == [512]
+
+    # Selected from the target's groups, the draft keeps 128-token pages.
+    from_target = prepare_kernel_block_sizes(kv_cache_config, groups)
+    assert from_target == [128]
+    draft_groups, draft_sizes, _ = init(
+        active_layer_names={"draft"}, kernel_block_sizes=from_target
+    )
+    assert draft_sizes == [128]
+    assert [g.kernel_block_size for g in draft_groups[0]] == [128]
+
+
+def test_packed_cache_keeps_allocation_block_size(init):
+    # Block-outermost packing is never split group-wide: the allocation keeps
+    # 512-token blocks and each backend subdivides its own layers' pages.
+    groups, target_sizes, kv_cache_config = init(
+        packed=True, draft_layer_names={"draft"}
+    )
+    assert target_sizes == [512]
+
+    # The draft gets the allocation size, not the target backend's 128.
+    from_target = prepare_kernel_block_sizes(kv_cache_config, groups)
+    assert from_target == [512]
+    _, draft_sizes, _ = init(
+        packed=True, active_layer_names={"draft"}, kernel_block_sizes=from_target
+    )
+    assert draft_sizes == [512]
